findings.title: Expected state is computed by the Game.play code under test, and no edge taps are covered
findings.failure_scenario: The tests build expectations with `$0.game.play(at:)`, the same code the reducer calls. If Game.play regressed (for example, accepting a tap on an occupied cell), both sides change together and the test still passes. No test taps an occupied cell, taps after a win, or presses New game after a finished game, so GameFeature's handling of those taps is unpinned.
findings.evidence: GameFeatureTests.swift:11 `await store.send(.cellTapped(4)) { $0.game.play(at: 4) }`; GameFeature.swift:24 `state.game.play(at: index)`. The test's only edge is two different cells.
findings.fix: Assert literal board state, such as `$0.game.board[4] == .x`. Add a tap on an occupied cell and a New game after a win, with the expected state asserted explicitly.
findings.verification_note: I read GameFeatureTests.swift and GameFeature.swift (lines 20-31). The quoted code is there, but it's not a defect in the code under test. GameFeature's reducer does only two things: it passes `.cellTapped(index)` to `state.game.play(at: index)` and it replaces the game on `.newGameButtonTapped`. I traced the mutations a reducer bug could make, and the tests catch each one. Dropping the play call fails at line 11, because the expected state has a move and the actual state doesn't. Playing the wrong index, such as play(at: 0) or index+1, fails because the expected state uses the literal 4 and 0. Making New game a no-op fails at line 20. So the test does fail for any GameFeature bug. A Game.play regression, such as accepting a tap on an occupied cell, would go unnoticed here, but that is the TicTacToe engine's rule, which is imported via `@_exported import TicTacToe` and belongs in the engine's own tests. GameFeature has no edge-tap handling of its own to pin, because occupied-cell and post-win taps go through the same delegation. Using the engine call as the oracle in a TCA reducer test that only delegates is a style choice. It doesn't leave reducer behaviour unpinned. Nothing here goes wrong, so verified false. The run-viewer span start failed with a config error: both .swiftgate.toml and .git/swift-harness/config.toml exist.

notes:
GameFeature (AppCore, @Reducer): State{game: Game}, Action{cellTapped(Int), newGameButtonTapped}. AppCore re-exports TicTacToe (@_exported import) so AppUI/App need no Package.swift change. GameView(store: StoreOf<GameFeature>) in AppUI; ids game.cell.0-8 (label X/O/Empty), game.status, game.newGame. App root now GameFeature/GameView. GameFlowUITests/LaunchFlowUITests are build-only at slice and need ttt-engine merged to pass. Gate only builds the area (area.build-only nit); the unit tests were run locally via swift test (host-app issue noise, not verified green on the real engine). events span start failed with a config conflict (.swiftgate.toml and .git/swift-harness/config.toml both exist) so span is null.
